TaskMode.description: The closed Task mode vocabulary on the wire (KAN-S4-US4): whether a human or an agent executes the bounded work.

oneOf.description: Sid executes the work.
An agent executes the work under dispatch.

TaskSubtype.description: The closed Task subtype vocabulary on the wire (DR-TK-06): the seven bounded flavours of non-story work.

oneOf.description: Keeping the product and its operations running.
Finding out what is true before acting on it.
Bookkeeping and record-keeping work.
Learning without a deliverable committed up front.
Proving an approach before committing to it.
Moving work or data from one place to another.
Work done by hand, on purpose.

TicketBugQualification.description: One complete Bug qualification (DR-TK-09): the ten facts a Bug needs before it may leave draft, with the severity qualification assigned (DR-LC-13). Sent whole; qualification is one act.

criteria.description: The story-linked Acceptance Criteria, at least one.

expected_behaviour.description: The behaviour that should have happened.

reproduction.description: The reproduction steps or the failing test demonstrating the defect.

risk.description: What the defect puts at risk.

verification_steps.description: The Verification Steps, at least one.

TicketBugRecord.description: The Bug-specific body of a Ticket record: the quick-capture facts, the qualification once one exists, and the vendor-neutral collections the Bug carries (DR-TK-08 to DR-TK-10).

actual_behaviour.description: What the Bug records happening, as the reporter stated it.

evidence_ids.description: The identities of the Evidence Items this Bug carries (DR-TK-10).

external_references.description: The External References, in recording order (DR-TK-10).

occurrence_snapshots.description: The Occurrence Snapshots, in recording order (DR-TK-10).

qualification.description: The complete qualification, once one exists (DR-TK-09).

reporter_evidence.description: The evidence the reporter holds, as the reporter stated it.

TicketCriterion.description: One story-linked criterion a Ticket claims: an observable outcome and the User Stories it delivers, named like `CORE-S3-US6` or `S3-US6` (DR-TK-04, DR-PS-13).

outcome.description: The observable outcome the criterion states.

stories.description: The User Stories the criterion claims.

TicketExternalReference.description: One vendor-neutral External Reference a Bug carries (DR-TK-10): a URI naming an outside link, with an optional label.

label.description: The reference's label, when it carries one.

TicketKind.description: The closed Ticket kind vocabulary on the wire (DR-TK-01).

oneOf.description: A small vertical product slice of exactly one Spec.
A record of incorrect behaviour, with qualification evidence.
Bounded operational, investigative, or administrative work.

TicketOccurrenceSnapshot.description: One Occurrence Snapshot a Bug carries (DR-TK-10): the RFC 3339 moment one occurrence was observed and what was seen then.

observation.description: What was observed at that moment.

TicketPriority.description: The closed priority vocabulary on the wire (DR-LC-12): urgent, high, normal, low.

oneOf.description: Ahead of everything else.
Ahead of normal work.
The everyday order.
Behind normal work.

TicketRecord.description: The Ticket record as every client sees it: the Project it belongs to, the number that Project minted, the kind whose schema it carries, the kind-specific fields — a title for Bugs and Tasks, a slice and criteria for Implementations, the Bug body for a Bug, and for Tasks the subtype, mode, completion criteria, and optional timing — and the Execution Profile the assignment names, if it carries one.

bug.description: The Bug body, if this Ticket carries one.

completion.description: The Task's completion criteria; empty for every other kind.

criteria.description: The Implementation's story-linked criteria; empty for every other kind.

due.description: The Task's due date, if it carries one; RFC 3339 in UTC.

kind.description: The kind whose schema this Ticket carries.

mode.description: The Task's human-or-agent mode, if this Ticket carries one.

number.description: The number this Project minted for this Ticket; rendered with the Project's code, for example `CORE-T17`.

pinned_spec_version.description: The Spec content version an approved Ticket graph pinned this Ticket to, if one did (DR-DE-06); a pinned Ticket stays with its Spec and version.

profile.description: The Execution Profile this Ticket's assignment names, by its catalogue name. The reference keeps its name through every later catalogue change (DR-EP-05).

project_id.description: The Project this Ticket belongs to.

scheduled_for.description: The Task's one-time activation instant, if it carries one; RFC 3339 in UTC, stored for KAN-S11.

slice.description: The Implementation slice description, if this Ticket carries one.

spec_id.description: The Spec this Ticket attaches to, if it attaches to one.

subtype.description: The Task's subtype, if this Ticket carries one.

title.description: The Bug or Task title, if this Ticket carries one.

version.description: The aggregate version, for optimistic mutation checks.

TicketSeverity.description: The closed Bug severity vocabulary on the wire (DR-LC-13): critical, high, medium, low. Severity arrives only inside a qualification (DR-TK-09).

oneOf.description: Data loss, secret exposure, or unauthorised execution.
A failed approved criterion or workflow invariant.
Usable behaviour, wrongly shaped.
Cosmetic or local clarity.

TicketState.description: The closed Ticket lifecycle vocabulary on the wire (DR-LC-01): the canonical states in order, with the terminal states after them. Every Ticket is created into draft; the transition rules are the lifecycle slice's.

oneOf.description: Newly created; not yet qualified or planned.
Deliberately set aside.
Waiting on something outside the Ticket.
Qualified but unavailable until activation.
Free to execute when capacity allows.
Executing.
Under review.
Review approved, waiting to land.
Landing through the Seed Workspace.
Landed in full.
Terminal: will not execute.
Terminal: replaced by a reassignment Ticket.

TicketVerificationStep.description: One Verification Step a Ticket claims: the command or scripted procedure that demonstrates a criterion (DR-PS-15). Commands live here and never as criteria.

tickets.description: Every Ticket of the Project, oldest first, all lifecycle states included.
